Pharma Policy.url_match_title: India Is Insuring AYUSH Healthcare: What Can Africa Learn? - Modern Ghana
Pharma Policy.content:
For many years, debates about traditional, complementary and integrative medicine in Africa have centred on one major question: Who should regulate the practitioners?
That question is important, but my study of India’s healthcare system raises another equally important question: Who pays when patients choose traditional or complementary healthcare?
India’s experience with Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy—collectively known as AYUSH—provides an important lesson. India has moved beyond merely recognizing these systems and has progressively developed mechanisms through which qualifying AYUSH treatments can enter the health-insurance system. Private health insurance can also cover AYUSH treatment, subject to the particular policy and its conditions.
Recognition alone is not enough
A healthcare profession may be legally recognized, practitioners registered and clinics permitted to operate, yet patients may still finance consultations, medicines, investigations, therapies and procedures entirely out of pocket. This creates an important distinction between regulatory integration and financial integration.
Regulatory integration asks who is legally permitted to provide a healthcare service. Financial integration asks whether the healthcare financing system can pay for an eligible service when a patient needs it. India is increasingly addressing both questions.
AYUSH has entered India’s insurance architecture
India’s Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDAI) has developed a formal framework within which AYUSH treatment can be recognized for health-insurance purposes. In January 2024, IRDAI issued specific guidelines concerning AYUSH coverage, followed by a broader contemporary health-insurance regulatory framework.
This does not mean that every insurance policy automatically pays for every Ayurveda, naturopathy or other AYUSH treatment. Coverage remains connected to the particular insurance product, eligible treatment, facility and policy requirements. Regulatory inclusion therefore does not mean unlimited contractual entitlement.
Private insurance matters too
Another lesson for Africa is that complementary healthcare insurance does not necessarily have to begin with government. Private insurers in India provide AYUSH benefits in specified health-insurance products, subject to policy terms and eligibility requirements.
Private insurers, employer schemes and supplementary insurance products in Africa could therefore pilot carefully defined complementary-health benefits before governments contemplate wider public coverage.
India has developed benchmark prices
In May 2026, India’s Ministry of Ayush published revised benchmark rates and additional procedures for insurance coverage involving Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha, and Yoga and Naturopathy. The framework applies to cashless, reimbursement and settlement of treatment-expenditure claims.
India is therefore addressing practical questions such as what treatment is being provided, how it should be classified, what it should cost, where it should be delivered, what standards facilities should meet and how insurance claims should be settled.
Accreditation can affect payment
The 2026 framework differentiates reimbursement according to factors including accreditation status, hospital type, geographical classification and ward entitlement. This is significant because insurance can become an instrument for improving quality.
Better standards can lead to accreditation, which may improve reimbursement arrangements. Healthcare facilities therefore gain an economic incentive to strengthen clinical governance, documentation, staffing, infection prevention and patient safety.
Even certain Ayurveda procedures enter the framework
The insurance schedules extend beyond simple consultations and herbal medicines and include specified Ayurveda procedural and surgical specialties such as Shalya, Shalakya and Prasuti Tantra & Stree Roga.
However, insurance coverage must never be confused with professional authority. The appropriate sequence is qualification, competency, lawful scope, appropriate facility, eligible procedure, insurance authorization and reimbursement. An insurer cannot confer a clinical scope that a practitioner does not otherwise possess.
Popularity alone should not determine insurance coverage
Traditional and complementary medicine is widely used across Africa, but popularity alone is not sufficient justification for spending limited insurance resources. Professional recognition should also not automatically result in reimbursement for every intervention used by a profession.
Professional recognition and scientific evidence are different questions. Insurance decisions should consider safety, effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, appropriate indications and the ability to monitor outcomes.
Africa should not simply announce that traditional medicine is covered
A blanket declaration that traditional medicine is covered would be too vague. Policymakers would still have to determine whether coverage includes consultations, herbal medicines, acupuncture, naturopathic treatment, hydrotherapy, traditional bone setting, inpatient treatment or other services.
Different interventions involve different levels of evidence, risk, professional competency and cost. A responsible insurance framework should therefore determine coverage at the level of the defined healthcare service.
I propose an African insurance-readiness model
From my examination of India’s system, I propose the African TCIM Health Insurance Readiness Framework (ATHIRF). Before a traditional or complementary healthcare service becomes eligible for insurance, policymakers should examine the following domains:
Area
Question Africa should ask
Legal recognition
Is the profession or service legally recognized?
Regulation
Are practitioners properly registered?
Competency
Are education and clinical competencies standardized?
Scope
Is the practitioner’s scope clearly defined?
Facilities
Are appropriate facility standards established?
Evidence
Is there reasonable evidence of safety and effectiveness?
Coding
Can the treatment be clearly identified and coded?
Pricing
Can a reasonable reimbursement tariff be established?
Claims
Can insurers verify the practitioner, facility and treatment?
Outcomes
Can costs, outcomes, adverse events and fraud be monitored?
Source: Constructed by the Author (2026).
Not everything has to enter insurance at once
Africa could adopt a three-level approach. A green category could contain interventions for which practitioners are regulated, treatments standardized, facilities appropriate, evidence adequate and tariffs established. These could qualify for insurance.
An amber category could contain promising interventions where regulation exists but evidence, coding or economic evaluation remains incomplete. These could enter controlled pilot programmes. A red category would include interventions where qualifications are uncertain, treatments cannot be standardized, evidence is inadequate or claims cannot reliably be audited.
Insurance could transform complementary healthcare in Africa
Insurance requirements could encourage healthcare professions to improve. If insurers demand proper clinical records, practitioners must document treatment. If insurers require recognized qualifications, professional education must improve. If reimbursement depends on licensed facilities, clinics must meet standards. If treatments require codes, professions must standardize terminology. If payment depends on evidence, researchers must produce evidence.
Insurance can therefore become a powerful instrument for professionalization, quality assurance and accountability.
But India also gives Africa a warning
India’s system is evolving rather than complete. Coverage written into an insurance policy does not automatically guarantee easy access. Claims can still be disputed, hospitals need adequate documentation, insurers must determine medical necessity, patients need to understand their benefits and fraud must be controlled.
Africa should therefore learn from both India’s achievements and its implementation difficulties.
From recognition to financial integration
The development of a healthcare profession does not end when government agrees to regulate it. A mature pathway runs from recognition to regulation, education and competency, scope of practice, facility standards, evidence, accreditation, treatment coding, standardized tariffs, insurance coverage, claims monitoring and clinical and economic outcomes.
India’s contemporary AYUSH insurance framework demonstrates how far this process can develop. Africa should study the model critically and adapt relevant principles to local health systems.
Africa should begin the conversation
African policymakers should begin asking whether properly regulated and evidence-supported traditional and complementary healthcare interventions can eventually participate in national and private health-insurance systems. The objective should not be to place every traditional therapy on an insurance list, nor should Africa imitate India blindly.
The objective should be to build an African model based on patient safety, evidence, professional competency, cultural relevance, affordability and financial sustainability.
Perhaps the next chapter in the development of traditional, complementary and integrative healthcare in Africa should therefore not simply ask, “Who regulates us?” We should also begin asking: “When properly regulated and supported by evidence, how can these healthcare services become part of the financial architecture of universal health coverage?”
About the Author
Prof. Raphael Nyarkotey Obu is a Ghanaian naturopathic academic, researcher and lawyer whose scholarly interests include naturopathy, health law, health policy, professional regulation and the development of traditional, complementary and integrative healthcare in Africa.

Elizabeth Warren Blasts Trump, GOP Over Billionaire-Friendly Policies: 'Kicking 15 Million Americans Off Their Health Care'
Benzinga
22 hrs ago
S
en.
Elizabeth Warren
(D-Mass.) accused President
Donald Trump
and Republicans of putting millions of Americans' health coverage at risk, citing an estimate that their policies could result in 15 million people losing coverage.
Advertisement
Warren Targets GOP Health Care Cuts
On Saturday, Warren wrote on
X
, "Here's your daily reminder: Trump and Republicans are kicking 15 million Americans off their health care so that people like Mark Zuckerberg can buy another yacht."
Advertisement
Trump Administration Reverses Health Funding Moves
Earlier, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services said it would end the Medicare Part D Premium Stabilization Demonstration after 2026, potentially raising prescription drug costs for some seniors in 2027.
The program had provided an estimated $3.6 billion in subsidies in 2026. CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz defended the move, saying the market was being stabilized without the need for the "bailout."
Separately, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services rescinded a $10 billion freeze on child care and social services funding for California, Colorado, Illinois, Minnesota and New York.
The decision ended the January funding restrictions that had prompted the five states to sue the administration. A federal judge had previously blocked the freeze while the legal challenge continued.
Medicare for All Debate Gains Momentum
Rep.
Ro Khanna
(D-Calif.) cited a Yale analysis projecting that a Medicare-for-All-style system could save $1.04 trillion annually, or nearly 20% of U.S. health spending, through lower insurance and drug costs and reduced administrative waste.
He said the savings could support higher Medicare payments, cover $52 billion in unpaid hospital care and improve health care worker pay.
Sen.
Mark Kelly
(D-Ariz.) criticized Republican health care proposals, arguing that spending cuts could hurt access to affordable care. He called for lower costs and broader coverage, accusing Republicans of "gutting healthcare programs to give handouts to billionaires."
Sen.
Bernie Sanders
(I-Vt.) renewed his push for Medicare for All, calling the U.S. health system "broken" and arguing that health care should be a basic human right.
He cited a poll showing 64% support for Medicare for All and criticized insurers and drug companies for profiting from the system.
Meanwhile,
Mark Cuban
criticized the insurance industry, saying "most insurers aren't insurers" and accusing companies of profiting from gaps in health care contracts and weak oversight.

Pharma Policy.url_match_title: India Sets New Quality Standards for Semaglutide After Patent Expiry - Whalesbook
Pharma Policy.content:
The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission is developing a mandatory monograph to standardize the production of semaglutide. This move follows the drug’s patent expiry in March 2026 and the subsequent rise of affordable generic versions from companies like Sun Pharma and Dr. Reddy’s. It aims to ensure patient safety and product consistency in the rapidly growing Indian GLP-1 market.
The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC) has initiated the process of drafting a formal, legally binding monograph for semaglutide, the active ingredient in widely used diabetes and weight-loss medications. This new regulatory standard will define the exact requirements for identity, purity, and potency, providing a uniform testing protocol for manufacturers across the country.
This development comes as a direct response to the shifting landscape of the Indian pharmaceutical market. Following the expiry of the global patent for semaglutide on March 20, 2026, the market saw a surge in the launch of affordable generic alternatives. Major domestic pharmaceutical companies, including Sun Pharma, Zydus Lifesciences, Dr. Reddy's Laboratories, Mankind Pharma, Torrent Pharmaceuticals, and Glenmark Pharmaceuticals, have all entered this space, significantly expanding access to the drug.
The rapid growth of the GLP-1 segment—which includes drugs for weight management and diabetes—has been substantial. As of July 2026, the market reached a moving annual total of approximately ₹2,215 crore, marking a 235% increase compared to the previous year. With this rapid scaling, the introduction of a national monograph is intended to ensure that all manufacturers, regardless of their production methods, adhere to consistent safety and quality benchmarks.
Because semaglutide is a complex peptide molecule, it requires precise manufacturing conditions, including sophisticated cell culture techniques. Previously, manufacturers largely relied on internal protocols or international standards. By establishing indigenous IP monographs, the government aims to reduce testing costs and provide a clear regulatory framework for both domestic and multinational firms operating in India.
While the expansion of the market has made treatment more accessible, it has also introduced specific challenges. Regulatory bodies have previously raised concerns regarding the unsupervised use of prescription-only GLP-1 medications and misleading surrogate advertising. Additionally, the complexity of cold-chain logistics for injectable biologics poses a persistent risk for product efficacy. The new standards are expected to help state regulators identify and curb the entry of counterfeit or sub-standard products into the supply chain.
For investors and market observers, the key monitorable will be how effectively pharmaceutical companies align their production processes with these incoming standards. As the government continues to increase oversight, the focus remains on ensuring that the rapid increase in generic availability does not compromise patient safety or product efficacy.

Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Administrator Dr.
Mehmet Oz
touted the
Trump administration’s
efforts to lower prescription drug prices, arguing that Americans are beginning to see the impact of the administration’s most-favored-nation pricing agreements and the TrumpRx platform.
“This is just what the doctor ordered. This is the No. 1 issue that Americans fear about
healthcare
costs, because it comes out of their pocket. If you’re sitting at home right now, you go to a drugstore, because a doctor prescribed the medication, especially a branded product, that might change your life for the better, hopefully. One in three times, roughly, you will leave empty handed cause you can’t afford the medication,” Oz said on CBS News’s
Face the Nation
Sunday.

Oz emphasized that the cost of healthcare remains a major concern for Americans, particularly when expenses come directly out of their pockets. He also noted that patients are frequently forced to leave pharmacies without their prescriptions because they cannot afford them.

He argued that the administration’s efforts are changing that dynamic by addressing the disparity between what Americans pay for prescription drugs and what patients in other countries pay.

drug prices fell
0.8% in July and were down 3.1% from the previous year, marking the steepest annual decline in more than 60 years. The decline has coincided with the administration’s Most Favored Nation agreements and the February launch of TrumpRx.

Oz said the administration was careful not to dictate what pharmaceutical companies could charge, but instead sought to prevent Americans from paying substantially more than consumers abroad.
WHITE HOUSE ADDS GENERICS TO TRUMPRX
TrumpRx has also
expanded
since its February launch. In May, the administration added more than 600 generic medications through partnerships with Cost Plus Drugs, Amazon Pharmacy, and GoodRx, broadening the platform’s ability to connect consumers with lower-cost prescriptions.

Oz argued that the combination of international price matching and expanded access through TrumpRx could produce “seismic” savings for American patients.

Pharma Policy.url_match_title: Does Medicare Cover Statins? Here's What Seniors Need to Know - AOL.com
Pharma Policy.content:
A new study published in the
Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA)
revealed that 93 percent of adults aged 70 to 79
qualify for cholesterol-lowering statins
.  This study came after the American College of Cardiology and American Heart Association released
new 2026 cholesterol guidelines
earlier this year. The new guidelines have many seniors asking if they should be taking the medications, and wondering, if they  do qualify for statins, will the drugs be covered by Medicare? And if not, are there any other ways to get statins for less? We share everything you need to know below.
Have Diabetes? What Medicare Will and Won’t Cover, Plus Tips To Save Big
First, what are statins?
Statins are a prescription medication used to lower LDL or bad cholesterol, which can help reduce the risk of a heart attack or stroke. The medication
does have side effects
, including muscle aches, liver issues, cognitive changes and an increased risk of type 2 diabetes, but it's considered safe by most medical professionals.
Getty
What Medicare Covers for Heart Disease—and What It Doesn't
Does Medicare cover statins?
Medicare does cover statins for people whose prescriptions are covered by Medicare Advantage plans or by a standalone Part D prescription drug plan.
“Medicare beneficiaries diagnosed with high cholesterol and heart disease will find that Medicare prescription drug plans cover the most common statin medications, usually with a reasonable copay,” Whitney Stidom, vice president of consumer enablement at eHealth, an online health insurance marketplace, explains. “That coverage typically includes generic statin drugs such as atorvastatin, rosuvastatin and simvastatin, and copays can be as low as $0 when using the insurance carrier’s mail-order pharmacy for 90-day home deliveries. It’s worth noting, however, that brand-name statins may require prior authorization or step therapy [which is when insurance companies make patients try lower-cost medications before approving the originally prescribed one], depending on the rules of the beneficiary’s plan.”
She also notes that for people on Medicare Advantage plans, other programs can help them manage their cholesterol without medication, including a Chronic Condition Special Needs Plan, which is an insurance plan that can be tailored to people with severe heart disease.
“For Medicare beneficiaries diagnosed with heart disease, it may be helpful to opt for a specialized Medicare Advantage plan known as a Chronic Condition Special Needs Plan (C-SNP),” she says. “These plans are designed for beneficiaries with certain chronic conditions, offering coordinated care, specialized provider networks and more affordable access to prescription drugs to help people better manage cardiovascular disorders or chronic heart failure.”
Advertisement
What to do if your Medicare plan doesn't cover statins
If your Medicare plan doesn't cover statins, there are a few things you can do. The first is to pay full price for the medication, but that choice will most likely cost you quite a bit.
GoodRX reports
that 30 10-mg tablets can cost $47.60 on average.
The second is to see if your medication is included in any direct-to-consumer pharmacies like
TrumpRx
, Amazon Pharmacy, GoodRX, Hims & Hers, and Honeybee Health. Sometimes those companies offer medication at a lower price without insurance or give you a coupon that you can use to get them for less at your local pharmacy.
Getty
“For people enrolled solely in Original Medicare, which does not include prescription drug coverage, beneficiaries would be responsible for the full cost of statins. This is important to recognize, even for people who rarely visit a pharmacy,” Stidom says. “Prescription needs can change unexpectedly, and the risk of developing chronic conditions increases by age. In fact,
88 percent of Americans 65 and older
take at least one prescription medication, so it is important for Medicare beneficiaries to understand their current drug coverage and confirm it meets their needs now and in the future.”
Ready for more?
Subscribe to our YouTube channel
for video podcasts, health tips and uplifting stories designed for women 40, 50, 60 and beyond.
This content is not a substitute for professional medical advice or diagnosis. Always consult your physician before pursuing any treatment plan
.

Warren Targets GOP Health Care Cuts
On Saturday, Warren wrote on
X

Trump Administration Reverses Health Funding Moves
Earlier, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services said
it would end the Medicare Part D Premium
Stabilization Demonstration after 2026, potentially raising prescription drug costs for some seniors in 2027.
The program had provided an estimated $3.6 billion in subsidies in 2026. CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz defended the move, saying the market was being stabilized without the need for the "bailout."

renewed his push for Medicare for Al
l, calling the U.S. health system "broken" and arguing that health care should be a basic human right.
He cited a poll showing 64% support for Medicare for All and criticized insurers and drug companies for profiting from the system.
Meanwhile,

criticized the insurance industry, saying "most insurers aren’t insurers" and
accusing companies of profiting from gap
s in health care contracts and weak oversight.

Pharma Policy.url_match_title: "30,000 Won in Korea, 70,000 Won in Japan"—Koreans Fill Suitcases as Illegal Direct Purchases Soar - 아시아경제
Pharma Policy.content:
Illegal Direct Purchases of Wegovy and Mounjaro Surge
1,189 Cases Last Year, 4,155 in the First Half of This Year
"They say even after paying for the flight, you'll still make a profit if you buy 'Sushijaro' (an online slang term for the Japanese version of Mounjaro)."
The number of cases caught importing the anti-obesity drugs Wegovy and Mounjaro illegally from overseas has been soaring. Despite the government's efforts to ramp up enforcement due to concerns about misuse and safety risks, the stark price differences between countries and the plummeting value of the yen have triggered an explosion in attempts to smuggle these drugs via international mail or carried in travelers’ personal baggage.
An image generated by artificial intelligence (AI) to aid understanding of the article. ChatGPT
View original image
Surpassing Seven Times the Legitimate Imports... 'Direct International Mail Purchases' Are the Main Illegal Channel
According to the Korea Customs Service on August 24, there were a total of 4,155 detected cases of illegal importation of anti-obesity drugs such as Mounjaro and Wegovy from January to June this year. This is more than 3.5 times last year's total of 1,189 cases.
Looking at the trend since the drugs were launched domestically: there were only 4 cases in 2024, 1,189 in 2025, and 4,155 in the first half of this year, bringing the cumulative total to 5,348.
By contrast, during the same period, only 596 cases were processed through legitimate importers (14 in 2024, 191 in 2025, and 391 in the first half of 2026), indicating that illegal imports far outstrip legitimate supply—a distorted structure that is only worsening.
Obesity Treatment Drug Mounjaro. Reuters Yonhap News
View original image
By import route, illegal direct purchasing through international mail overwhelmingly dominated. Postal detections rose from just 2 cases in 2024 and 1,046 in 2025 to 3,489 in the first half of this year, representing 84.8% of total cumulative cases. This trend is attributed to the widespread practice of consumers purchasing directly from overseas websites and receiving the product by international mail.
Cases involving travelers’ hand-carried goods also increased during the same period: 1 in 2024, 134 in 2025, and 656 in the first half of this year. Shipments via express cargo were tallied at 1, 9, and 10 respectively.
As Much as Fourfold Price Difference... 'Sushijaro' Shopping Expeditions
The fundamental reason for the surge in illegal imports is the extreme price gap between countries. For a four-week supply of Mounjaro 2.5 mg, the lowest domestic price at a clinic in Korea is 290,000 won, whereas in Japan, it is about 74,000 won—roughly a quarter of the price in Korea. Even the high-dose 10 mg product costs 540,000 won in Korea, while it is only 294,000 won in Japan.
These price discrepancies are interpreted as resulting from differences in pricing systems and market environments. In Japan, Mounjaro is classified as a type 2 diabetes medication under the national health insurance pricing system, subject to government price control, and recent competition among online clinics has further driven prices down. By contrast, in Korea, anti-obesity drugs are non-reimbursed medications, so individual medical institutions can set prices freely.
Furthermore, the won-yen exchange rate has recently dropped into the 800-won range, and growing demand for high-dose products that are hard to obtain domestically is fueling overseas purchases.
A sold-out notice posted on a medicine container at a pharmacy in Seoul city. Photo by Yonhap News
View original image
Online, information about how to circumvent the law for illegal importation is being openly shared. Reviews include, "If you buy a three-month supply of Sushijaro, you cover your airfare," "Here's how to avoid customs declarations," and "Carry-on baggage is not fully inspected, so it’s fine."
Recently, a buyer identified as Mr. A, who purchased a two-month supply of Mounjaro in Japan, said, "I put it in my backpack instead of a handheld bag, fearing it would look suspicious, and fortunately I wasn't caught." Some clinics in Japan are even targeting Korean customers by providing Korean-language guidance, messaging, and interpretation services through KakaoTalk.
Crackdowns Are Being Strengthened, But Practical Challenges Remain
According to current Korea Customs Service import clearance regulations, up to six bottles or a three-month dose of regular pharmaceuticals may be brought in for personal use. However, Mounjaro and Wegovy have been designated as "hazardous drugs" by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, so imports are completely banned without a waiver recommendation letter. Customs authorities are now strictly policing imports of these products, regardless of quantity, in accordance with notifications from the drug safety ministry; any products caught at clearance are withheld and then destroyed in full.
A representative from Korea Customs Service stated, "Unauthorized importation of Wegovy or Mounjaro is a serious violation under the Customs Act," and added, "We will thoroughly block the illegal inflow of hazardous pharmaceuticals at the border."
Outside view of the Korea Customs Service building. Korea Customs Service
View original image
However, simply blocking imports at customs cannot fully curb the soaring import demand. Thoroughly inspecting all travelers' hand-carry baggage is unrealistically difficult, and even if items are seized, most are just confiscated and destroyed, as punitive provisions remain insufficient.

Pharma Associations.url_match_title: [Exclusive] Daewoong Pharmaceutical Enters Maternal Nutrition Supplement Market in Partnership with Mamitok - 아시아경제
Pharma Associations.content:
Targeting Early-Stage Expecting Mothers Directly
Leveraging a Platform with 1.5 Million Users
Daewoong Pharmaceutical is making a full-fledged entry into the maternal nutrition supplement market. The company plans to target this market, which is currently dominated by foreign pharmaceutical firms, by partnering with a pregnancy and parenting platform.
According to the pharmaceutical industry on August 24, Daewoong Pharmaceutical is expected to launch a maternal nutrition supplement co-developed with Mamitok as early as next month. Mamitok operates a pregnancy and parenting platform based on an application (app) that provides information related to pregnancy, childbirth, parenting, ultrasound image management, and community and shopping features. The app has a total of 1.5 million registered users and approximately 350,000 monthly active users.
Daewoong Pharmaceutical plans to secure distribution channels quickly by leveraging Mamitok, which will help it rapidly gain market presence. Since users can view and share ultrasound images taken at obstetrics and gynecology clinics, Mamitok attracts a relatively high number of consumers in the early stages of pregnancy, a key advantage Daewoong Pharmaceutical believes will enable customized marketing.
Based on consultation with obstetric specialists, Daewoong Pharmaceutical will introduce a product lineup that allows convenient intake of key nutrients necessary during pregnancy and breastfeeding. The company intends to begin sales through the Mamitok store and other channels.
View original image
The Korean maternal nutrition supplement market is currently led by over-the-counter products from global pharmaceutical companies such as Bayer's Elevit and Pfizer's Centrum Prenatal. While domestic players such as CHA Bio F&C with Motherscare (a CHA Biotech Group affiliate) and Chong Kun Dang with Goun Mother have entered the market, the industry believes that foreign pharmaceutical companies still hold the dominant position.
The maternal nutrition supplement market is regarded in the industry as a "long-tail market." Since there is virtually no repeat purchase and customers leave once the pregnancy or breastfeeding period ends, the consumer base is replaced in its entirety every year. One industry official noted, "While it's difficult to build cumulative brand awareness, businesses that reach early-stage consumers first can secure new opportunities each time." It is believed that Daewoong Pharmaceutical's focus on securing distribution channels is closely related to this market structure.
Recently, Daewoong Pharmaceutical has been actively strengthening its health functional foods business. The company began supplying products to Daiso as soon as the retailer started carrying health functional foods last year, and expanded its distribution by offering 12 new products to the convenience store chain 7-Eleven. At the regular shareholders' meeting this March, the company added the manufacture of health functional foods to its articles of incorporation and acquired a factory in Hoengseong, Gangwon Province, thereby securing its own manufacturing capabilities.

Pharmaceutical Desiccant Strips Market to Reach Index 183 by 2035 on Biologics and Regulatory Demands
Abstract
According to the latest IndexBox report on the global
Pharmaceutical Desiccant Strips market
, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture.
The global pharmaceutical desiccant strips market is set to record a steady growth trajectory over the 2026-2035 forecast period, supported by the expanding output of moisture-sensitive solid oral dosage forms, the rapid uptake of biologics and high-potency compounds, and tightening regulatory expectations around packaging integrity and product stability. Desiccant strips, which are laminated moisture-absorbing formats inserted into pharmaceutical containers, are increasingly preferred over loose canisters and pouches due to their compact design, ease of automated handling, and compatibility with high-speed packaging lines. The market is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 6.2% between 2026 and 2035, with the market index rising to 183 by 2035 (2025=100). Demand is particularly strong in North America and Europe, where regulatory scrutiny is highest, while Asia-Pacific emerges as the fastest-growing region on the back of expanding generic drug manufacturing and clinical trial activity. Key trends include the shift from silica gel to molecular sieve strips for ultra-low humidity applications, the integration of color-indicating and smart tracer technologies, and growing pressure for recyclable and bio-based strip formats. However, suppliers face challenges from raw material cost volatility, lengthy qualification cycles, and the need for continuous investment in regulatory compliance. This report provides a detailed analysis of market size, demand structure, supply chain dynamics, competitive landscape, and forecast to 2035, offering actionable insights for manufacturers, distributors, and procurement teams.
The baseline scenario for the pharmaceutical desiccant strips market points to sustained expansion through 2035, with global consumption rising at a CAGR of 6.2% in volume terms. This growth is anchored in the structural increase in pharmaceutical production, particularly of tablets, capsules, and lyophilized products that require strict moisture control. The market is also benefiting from the ongoing shift toward molecular sieve strips, which offer superior adsorption at low humidity and are increasingly specified for biologics, diagnostic kits, and high-potency compounds. Regulatory frameworks such as USP , EU GMP Annex 1, and FDA 21 CFR Part 211 continue to raise the bar for packaging integrity, compelling manufacturers to adopt validated desiccant solutions. The competitive landscape remains concentrated among a handful of established players with qualified dossiers, creating high barriers to entry and stable pricing. Regional demand is led by North America, which accounts for 35% of global consumption, followed by Europe at 28% and Asia-Pacific at 25%. The latter is expected to post the fastest growth, driven by the expansion of domestic pharmaceutical manufacturing in China and India, as well as increasing clinical trial activity. While the market faces headwinds from raw material price volatility and the 12-18 month supplier qualification process, the overall outlook is positive, with innovation in smart and sustainable desiccant formats opening new application areas. The forecast assumes no major disruptions to global supply chains and a continuation of current regulatory trends.
Demand Drivers and Constraints
Primary Demand Drivers
Expansion of moisture-sensitive solid oral dosage forms in emerging markets
Increasing regulatory emphasis on packaging integrity and product stability
Shift from silica gel to molecular sieve strips for ultra-low humidity applications
Growth of biologics, high-potency compounds, and lyophilized products
Rising demand for color-indicating and smart desiccant strips for anti-counterfeiting
Expansion of clinical trial activities and diagnostic kit production
Potential Growth Constraints
Raw material cost volatility for silica gel, molecular sieves, and barrier films
Lengthy and costly supplier qualification cycles (12-18 months)
Energy-intensive drying and activation processes exposing margins to energy prices
Competition from alternative moisture control solutions such as canisters and pouches
Stringent regulatory compliance requiring continuous investment in validation and documentation
Demand Structure by End-Use Industry
Tablet and Capsule Bottles (estimated share: 35%)
Tablet and capsule bottles represent the largest end-use segment for pharmaceutical desiccant strips, accounting for 35% of global demand. The segment is driven by the sheer volume of solid oral dosage forms produced worldwide, particularly in emerging markets where generic drug manufacturing is expanding rapidly. Desiccant strips are preferred in this segment due to their low profile, which minimizes headspace in bottles and allows for higher fill volumes. The trend toward molecular sieve strips is gaining traction here, as they provide more consistent low-humidity protection for moisture-sensitive APIs. Through 2035, demand will be supported by the increasing prevalence of chronic diseases requiring long-term medication, as well as the growing adoption of unit-dose packaging. Key demand-side indicators include pharmaceutical production indices, prescription volumes, and the rate of new drug approvals. Major companies in this segment include Clariant, Multisorb, and Desiccare, which supply validated strips to major pharmaceutical manufacturers. Current trend: Steady growth driven by solid oral dosage expansion.
Major trends:
Shift to molecular sieve strips for enhanced moisture protection, Integration of color-indicating technology for visual integrity checks, Adoption of recyclable and bio-based strip materials, and Increasing use of automated packaging lines requiring precise strip dimensions.
Representative participants:
Clariant AG, Multisorb Technologies, Desiccare, Inc, Süd-Chemie AG, and Desican Inc.
Diagnostic Kit Packaging (estimated share: 20%)
Diagnostic kit packaging is a fast-growing segment for pharmaceutical desiccant strips, driven by the proliferation of rapid diagnostic tests, including lateral flow assays and molecular diagnostics. These kits often contain moisture-sensitive reagents and test strips that require strict humidity control to ensure accuracy and shelf life. Desiccant strips are integrated into the packaging to maintain low humidity without interfering with the kit's compact design. The segment is expected to grow at a CAGR of 8-10% through 2035, outpacing the overall market, as the demand for home-based and point-of-care testing continues to rise. The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the importance of reliable diagnostics, and this has led to sustained investment in diagnostic manufacturing capacity. Key demand drivers include the expansion of decentralized testing, the development of multiplexed assays, and regulatory requirements for kit stability. Major companies supplying desiccant strips for this segment include Multisorb, Clariant, and Desiccare, which offer customized strip formats that fit into small diagnostic pouches and cassettes. Current trend: Rapid growth amid expanding point-of-care testing.
Major trends:
Miniaturization of desiccant strips for compact diagnostic devices, Integration of RFID tracers for supply chain tracking, Use of molecular sieves for ultra-low humidity in sensitive assays, and Growing demand for ready-to-use strips with pre-validated performance.
Representative participants:
Multisorb Technologies, Clariant AG, Desiccare, Inc, W.R. Grace & Co, and Desican Inc.
Medical Device Packaging (estimated share: 18%)
Medical device packaging is a significant end-use segment for pharmaceutical desiccant strips, particularly for devices that are sensitive to moisture, such as diagnostic devices, implantable sensors, and electronic components. These devices often require low-humidity environments to prevent corrosion, degradation, or malfunction. Desiccant strips are used in primary and secondary packaging to maintain the required humidity levels during storage and transport. The segment is growing at a steady pace, supported by the increasing complexity of medical devices and the expansion of home healthcare. Regulatory standards such as ISO 11607 and FDA guidance on packaging validation drive the demand for high-quality, validated desiccant solutions. Through 2035, the segment will benefit from the growth of minimally invasive procedures and the increasing use of connected devices that contain sensitive electronics. Key demand indicators include medical device production indices, regulatory approvals, and the trend toward single-use devices. Major companies in this segment include Clariant, Multisorb, and Desiccare, which provide strips that meet stringent biocompatibility and extractables requirements. Current trend: Moderate growth driven by sterile device requirements.
Major trends:
Use of desiccant strips in combination with barrier films for enhanced protection, Adoption of molecular sieve strips for high-value electronic devices, Integration of humidity indicators for visual verification, and Growing demand for custom-sized strips for unique device geometries.
Representative participants:
Clariant AG, Multisorb Technologies, Desiccare, Inc, W.R. Grace & Co, and Absortech AB.
Bulk Drug Substance Containers (estimated share: 12%)
Bulk drug substance containers, including drums and intermediate bulk containers, require effective moisture control to protect active pharmaceutical ingredients during storage and transport. Desiccant strips are used in these containers to maintain low humidity and prevent hydrolysis or degradation of moisture-sensitive APIs. This segment accounts for 12% of the market and is driven by the globalization of pharmaceutical supply chains, where APIs are often manufactured in one region and formulated in another. The need for long-term stability during transit and storage is critical, especially for high-potency and biologics. The segment is expected to grow in line with the overall market, with a CAGR of around 6% through 2035. Key demand drivers include the expansion of contract manufacturing, the increasing complexity of APIs, and regulatory requirements for stability data. Major companies supplying desiccant strips for bulk containers include Clariant, Multisorb, and Desiccare, which offer large-format strips that can be easily inserted into drums and liners. Current trend: Steady growth with focus on large-scale moisture control.
Major trends:
Development of high-capacity strips for large containers, Use of molecular sieves for ultra-low humidity in sensitive APIs, Integration with humidity monitoring systems for real-time data, and Growing demand for strips that comply with food-contact and pharmaceutical regulations.
Representative participants:
Clariant AG, Multisorb Technologies, Desiccare, Inc, W.R. Grace & Co, and Sorbchem India Pvt. Ltd.
Laboratory Reagent Packaging (estimated share: 15%)
Laboratory reagent packaging is a dynamic segment for pharmaceutical desiccant strips, driven by the increasing demand for diagnostic reagents, research chemicals, and analytical standards. These reagents are often hygroscopic and require strict moisture control to maintain their activity and shelf life. Desiccant strips are used in packaging for vials, bottles, and pouches to protect the reagents from humidity. The segment is growing at a faster pace than the overall market, with a CAGR of 7-8% through 2035, supported by the expansion of pharmaceutical R&D, the growth of the biotechnology sector, and the increasing use of point-of-care diagnostics. The trend toward personalized medicine and companion diagnostics is also driving demand for specialized reagent packaging. Key demand indicators include R&D spending, the number of clinical trials, and the production of diagnostic kits. Major companies in this segment include Clariant, Multisorb, and Desiccare, which provide strips that meet the stringent purity and performance requirements of laboratory applications. Current trend: Rapid growth driven by R&D and diagnostic reagent demand.
Major trends:
Use of high-purity desiccants to avoid contamination, Integration of color-indicating strips for quick verification, Adoption of molecular sieves for ultra-dry environments, and Growing demand for small-format strips for microcentrifuge tubes and vials.
Representative participants:
Clariant AG, Multisorb Technologies, Desiccare, Inc, W.R. Grace & Co, and Desican Inc.

Regional Dynamics
Asia-Pacific (estimated share: 25%)
Asia-Pacific is the fastest-growing region, driven by expanding pharmaceutical manufacturing in China and India, increasing clinical trial activity, and rising demand for generic drugs. The region is also becoming a key production hub for desiccant strips, with local suppliers gaining share. Growth is supported by government initiatives to boost domestic drug production and improve packaging standards. Direction: Fastest growth.
North America (estimated share: 35%)
North America remains the largest market, driven by a mature pharmaceutical industry, high regulatory standards, and the presence of major desiccant strip manufacturers. The region is a leader in adopting advanced technologies such as molecular sieve strips and smart desiccants. Demand is supported by the growth of biologics and the increasing focus on packaging integrity. Direction: Largest market.
Europe (estimated share: 28%)
Europe is a mature market with steady growth, driven by stringent regulatory requirements and a strong pharmaceutical sector. The region is a hub for innovative packaging solutions, with a focus on sustainability and recyclability. Demand is supported by the expansion of biopharmaceutical manufacturing and the increasing use of desiccant strips in diagnostic kits. Direction: Steady growth.
Latin America (estimated share: 6%)
Latin America is a smaller market but is growing steadily, driven by the expansion of pharmaceutical production in Brazil and Mexico. The region is increasingly adopting international packaging standards, which is boosting demand for high-quality desiccant strips. Growth is supported by the rising prevalence of chronic diseases and the growth of the generic drug market. Direction: Moderate growth.
Middle East & Africa (estimated share: 6%)
The Middle East and Africa region is an emerging market with growing pharmaceutical manufacturing, particularly in the Gulf states and South Africa. The region is investing in healthcare infrastructure and local drug production, which is driving demand for moisture control solutions. Growth is supported by increasing regulatory alignment with international standards and the expansion of distribution networks. Direction: Emerging growth.

General News
Ghana to establish pharmaceutical industrial park to boost local production
On
Aug 23, 2026
Share
WhatsApp
Facebook
Twitter
Linkedin
Email
Ghana is set to establish a pharmaceutical industrial park to attract local and international manufacturers and strengthen domestic production of medicines, medical devices and other health-related products.
The project, being developed under the government’s 24-Hour Economy initiative, is expected to provide an integrated ecosystem for pharmaceutical manufacturing, medical device production, herbal medicine, research and development, and related industries.
Ms Kafui Linda Abbah-Foli, Head of Project Development, 24-Hour Economy, disclosed this at the opening of the 2026 China-West Africa Medical and Health Industry Expo and AI Deployment and Project Cooperation Summit in Accra.
She said the proposed park would address some of the major constraints facing manufacturers and entrepreneurs, particularly access to land and reliable bulk infrastructure.
“We are not just building a factory; we are building an ecosystem,” she said, explaining that the development would provide roads, electricity, water, wastewater and effluent treatment facilities required for pharmaceutical production.
She said about 2,000 acres of land had been identified in the Shai-Osudoku District for the project, with pre-feasibility studies already completed.
According to her, the project had an anchor investor and a pipeline of potential tenants, including existing pharmaceutical manufacturers in Ghana and international companies from India, China and the United States.
She added that Ghanaian health professionals in the diaspora had also expressed interest in the project.
Ms Abbah-Foli said the project development activities were expected to be completed by the end of the year, after which a full feasibility study, detailed design and master planning would be undertaken.
She said the development would also include a township and housing facilities for workers, with the ambition of supporting up to 20,000 people within its first five years of operation.
The Head of Project Development said the initiative was partly informed by Ghana’s dependence on imports, noting that the country currently imported about 70 per cent of its pharmaceutical needs.
She said Ghana also imported most of the active pharmaceutical ingredients and excipients used in local pharmaceutical production.
“The goal is to ensure that we build a park that will cater for the whole value chain,” she said, adding that the initiative would help Ghana become more self-sufficient in the production of essential medicines and health products.
She said the project was also intended to strengthen the country’s resilience against future health emergencies such as the COVID-19 pandemic.
Ms Abbah-Foli said land acquisition remained one of the potential challenges to the project but noted that the 24-Hour Economy programme had introduced a participatory land acquisition model.
Under the model, she explained, traditional authorities and land-owning communities would be encouraged to become shareholders in the project and benefit through dividends and rental income.
She said that approach would ensure that communities were active participants in the development and benefited directly from the economic opportunities it created.
She said Ghana’s changing disease burden, including the increasing prevalence of non-communicable diseases such as stroke and diabetes, made domestic pharmaceutical production even more important.
She said attracting manufacturers to produce medicines for such conditions locally would reduce dependence on imports and, in the long term, help reduce pressure on the national health bill.
Ms Foli speaking at the summit noted that Ghana must look beyond the provision of healthcare and focus on the entire health value chain, including the local production of medicines, medical equipment, supplies and health technologies.
Ghana offered significant opportunities for investors, manufacturers, medical technology companies and research institutions seeking a destination for production, research, innovation and technology transfer she stated.
She urged stakeholders to position Ghana not merely as a market for health products but as a centre for manufacturing, research, innovation and technology development.
The summit brings together stakeholders from Ghana, China and other parts of West Africa to explore opportunities in medical and health industry development, artificial intelligence, technology transfer, investment and project cooperation.
The speakers said stronger collaboration among government, industry, academia, research institutions and international investors would be critical to building a competitive health manufacturing sector capable of creating jobs, generating economic value and improving Ghana’s health security.
Source: GNA

Rubber-Lined Metal Closures Market Demand to Accelerate by 2035 on Pharmaceutical Vial Packaging Growth
Abstract
According to the latest IndexBox report on the global
Rubber-Lined Metal Closures market
, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture.
The global rubber-lined metal closures market is entering a period of sustained expansion, with demand projected to grow at a compound annual rate of 5-7% from 2026 to 2035. This growth is underpinned by the rapid scaling of biologics and vaccine production, which requires high-integrity sealing for parenteral vials and diagnostic containers. At the same time, premium food and beverage brands are increasingly adopting rubber-lined metal closures to enhance product freshness, tamper evidence, and consumer trust. The market is characterized by a bipolar geographic structure: mature regions such as North America and Europe prioritize regulatory compliance and high-quality closures for pharmaceutical and specialty applications, while Asia-Pacific serves as both the dominant manufacturing hub and the fastest-growing consumption center. China alone accounts for an estimated 35-40% of global manufacturing capacity, and the region captures 45-50% of world demand. Premium and specialty variants, including custom elastomer liners and tamper-evident designs, represent 30-35% of market value despite comprising only 20-25% of unit volume, reflecting the value-added nature of innovation in this segment. Sustainability mandates, particularly in Europe, are driving the development of recyclable and reduced-metal closures, with early-adopter regions already seeing 10-15% of new product launches featuring eco-design principles. Private-label and contract-manufactured closures are also gaining traction, especially in emerging markets where brand owners seek cost-optimized, certified solutions without internal production. This report provides a comprehensive analysis of market size, demand structure, supply capability, trade flows, pricing, and competitive landscape, offering a data-driven
The baseline scenario for the rubber-lined metal closures market points to steady, above-GDP growth through 2035, with the market index rising from 100 in 2025 to approximately 170 by 2035, reflecting a CAGR of 5-7%. This growth is anchored in the pharmaceutical segment, where the expansion of biologics, vaccines, and diagnostic kits is driving demand for high-integrity closures that ensure hermetic seals and compatibility with automated filling lines. The food and beverage segment, particularly premium and specialty products, is also contributing to volume growth as consumers prioritize freshness and safety. Geographically, Asia-Pacific will remain the largest market, supported by its manufacturing base and rising domestic consumption, while North America and Europe will see moderate but stable growth, with a focus on regulatory compliance and sustainability. The market will face headwinds from raw material price volatility, with steel and aluminum prices having fluctuated 20-30% over 2020-2025, and from regulatory complexity that adds 10-20% to production costs for smaller manufacturers. Supplier qualification bottlenecks, with lead times of 12-16 weeks for new certified closures, will continue to constrain supply flexibility during demand surges. Despite these challenges, the market is expected to benefit from the ongoing shift toward eco-design, the growth of private-label and contract manufacturing, and the increasing adoption of tamper-evident and leak-proof closures in e-commerce and retail channels. The forecast assumes no major disruptions to global trade flows or unprecedented regulatory changes, and it incorporates the gradual adoption of recyclable materials as a differentiating factor.
Demand Drivers and Constraints
Primary Demand Drivers
Expansion of pharmaceutical vial packaging for biologics and vaccines
Rising demand for premium food and beverage packaging with enhanced seal integrity
Growth of e-commerce and retail channels requiring tamper-evident and leak-proof closures
Sustainability mandates driving development of recyclable and reduced-metal closures
Increasing adoption of private-label and contract-manufactured closures in emerging markets
Technological advancements in elastomer liners and coating for improved performance
Potential Growth Constraints
Volatility in raw material costs for steel, aluminum, and specialty elastomers
Stringent regulatory compliance across FDA, EU 1935/2004, and pharmacopeial standards
Supplier qualification bottlenecks with lead times of 12-16 weeks for new certified closures
Competition from alternative closure materials such as plastic and cork
Environmental concerns regarding metal and rubber composite recyclability
Demand Structure by End-Use Industry
Pharmaceutical and Healthcare (estimated share: 35%)
The pharmaceutical segment is the primary growth engine for rubber-lined metal closures, driven by the expansion of parenteral vials, diagnostic containers, and vaccine packaging. The shift toward biologics and personalized medicine requires closures that provide a hermetic seal, compatibility with automated filling lines, and resistance to contamination. Demand-side indicators include the number of FDA-approved biologics, vaccine production volumes, and the growth of contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs). Through 2035, the segment is expected to grow at 7-9% annually, supported by the increasing prevalence of chronic diseases and the global push for healthcare infrastructure. The need for tamper-evident and child-resistant features also adds value, with premium closures gaining share. Regulatory compliance with pharmacopeial standards (USP, EP) is critical, and manufacturers that can offer validated, high-integrity solutions will capture premium pricing. The trend toward single-use systems and pre-filled syringes may impact closure design, but rubber-lined metal closures remain essential for multi-dose vials and lyophilized products. Current trend: Fastest-growing segment, driven by biologics and vaccine production.
Major trends:
Rise of biologics and biosimilars requiring high-integrity sealing, Adoption of ready-to-use (RTU) closures for aseptic filling, Increasing demand for tamper-evident and child-resistant designs, and Growth of contract manufacturing and outsourcing in pharma packaging.
Representative participants:
West Pharmaceutical Services, Inc, AptarGroup, Inc, Stevanato Group, Gerresheimer AG, and Schott AG.
Food and Beverage (estimated share: 30%)
In the food and beverage sector, rubber-lined metal closures are used for premium products such as craft beverages, sauces, jams, and specialty oils, where seal integrity and brand perception are paramount. The growth of e-commerce and direct-to-consumer channels has increased the need for leak-proof and tamper-evident closures that can withstand shipping and handling. Demand-side indicators include the volume of premium packaged foods, the expansion of craft beverage production, and the shift toward glass packaging for sustainability. Through 2035, the segment is expected to grow at 4-6% annually, with a notable shift toward eco-design and recyclable materials. Consumers are increasingly willing to pay for packaging that preserves freshness and reduces waste, driving adoption of closures with oxygen scavengers or enhanced barrier properties. Private-label brands are also upgrading their packaging to compete with national brands, creating opportunities for cost-effective, certified closures. The foodservice and institutional channel, including bulk packaging, adds a steady base of demand for standard closures, while retail and e-commerce channels favor premium and specialty variants. Current trend: Steady growth driven by premiumization and e-commerce packaging.
Major trends:
Premiumization of food and beverage packaging, Growth of e-commerce and direct-to-consumer sales, Sustainability and recyclability of closure materials, and Adoption of oxygen-scavenging and barrier technologies.
Representative participants:
Crown Holdings Inc, Silgan Holdings Inc, Guala Closures Group, Amcor plc, and Bericap GmbH & Co. KG.
Industrial and B2B (estimated share: 20%)
The industrial and B2B segment encompasses closures for chemical containers, paints, coatings, lubricants, and other specialty products that require corrosion-resistant and leak-proof sealing. Rubber-lined metal closures are preferred for their durability and compatibility with aggressive contents. Demand is tied to industrial production indices, construction activity, and automotive output. Through 2035, this segment is expected to grow at 3-5% annually, supported by the recovery of manufacturing and infrastructure spending. The trend toward safer and more sustainable packaging is driving the adoption of closures with improved chemical resistance and reduced environmental impact. B2B buyers prioritize reliability and cost-effectiveness, often sourcing from contract manufacturers or private-label suppliers. The replacement and recurring demand for closures in maintenance and aftermarket channels adds a stable revenue stream. Key demand-side indicators include the volume of industrial chemicals produced, the number of packaging regulations, and the growth of the paint and coatings industry. Current trend: Stable demand from chemical, paint, and lubricant packaging.
Major trends:
Increasing demand for corrosion-resistant and chemical-compatible closures, Growth of infrastructure and construction activities, Adoption of sustainable and recyclable packaging in industrial sectors, and Expansion of aftermarket and replacement demand.
Representative participants:
RPC Group (Berry Global), Closure Systems International (CSI), Alcopack S.A, Nippon Closures Co., Ltd, and Toyo Seikan Group Holdings, Ltd.
Retail and E-commerce (estimated share: 10%)
The retail and e-commerce segment covers closures for consumer packaged goods sold through online and brick-and-mortar channels. The surge in e-commerce has heightened the need for closures that prevent leakage, tampering, and contamination during transit. Rubber-lined metal closures offer a premium feel and enhanced protection, making them popular for cosmetics, nutraceuticals, and specialty foods sold online. Demand-side indicators include the growth of online grocery sales, the expansion of direct-to-consumer brands, and the increasing consumer focus on packaging safety. Through 2035, this segment is expected to grow at 6-8% annually, outpacing traditional retail. The trend toward unboxing experiences and premium packaging is driving demand for aesthetically pleasing and functional closures. Private-label and contract-manufactured closures are gaining share as smaller brands seek cost-effective solutions without compromising quality. The need for tamper-evident features is particularly strong in e-commerce, where products are handled multiple times before reaching the consumer. Current trend: Rapid growth driven by online shopping and tamper-evident requirements.
Major trends:
Growth of online grocery and direct-to-consumer sales, Increasing demand for tamper-evident and leak-proof closures, Premiumization of packaging for unboxing experiences, and Rise of private-label and contract-manufactured closures.
Representative participants:
Silgan Holdings Inc, Guala Closures Group, Amcor plc, United Caps Luxembourg S.A, and Mold-Rite Plastics (Pretium Packaging).
Foodservice and Institutional (estimated share: 5%)
The foodservice and institutional segment includes closures for bulk food containers, catering supplies, and hospitality packaging. These applications require durable, easy-to-use closures that maintain product freshness and withstand frequent handling. Demand is linked to the performance of the foodservice industry, including restaurants, hotels, and institutional catering. Through 2035, this segment is expected to grow at 3-4% annually, recovering from pandemic-related disruptions and benefiting from the expansion of delivery and takeaway services. The trend toward portion control and single-serve packaging is driving demand for smaller closures, while sustainability initiatives are pushing for recyclable materials. Rubber-lined metal closures are preferred for their seal integrity and compatibility with high-speed filling lines. The replacement and recurring demand from maintenance and aftermarket channels provides a stable base. Key demand-side indicators include the number of foodservice establishments, the volume of bulk food distribution, and the growth of the hospitality sector. Current trend: Moderate growth driven by bulk packaging and hospitality demand.
Major trends:

Regional Dynamics
Asia-Pacific (estimated share: 48%)
Asia-Pacific leads global demand and production, with China contributing 35-40% of manufacturing capacity. Rapid industrialization, expanding pharmaceutical and food sectors, and rising e-commerce drive growth. The region is expected to maintain a CAGR of 6-8% through 2035, with India and Southeast Asia emerging as key consumption centers. Direction: Dominant and fastest-growing.
North America (estimated share: 22%)
North America is a mature market emphasizing high-quality, compliant closures for pharmaceutical and premium food applications. The region benefits from strong biologics and vaccine production, with growth of 4-5% annually. Sustainability and eco-design are gaining traction, particularly in the US and Canada. Direction: Stable growth with regulatory focus.
Europe (estimated share: 20%)
Europe is a leader in sustainability and regulatory compliance, with early adoption of recyclable and reduced-metal closures. The market is mature, growing at 3-4% annually, driven by premium food and beverage packaging and pharmaceutical demand. EU regulations on packaging waste are shaping product innovation. Direction: Moderate growth with sustainability leadership.
Latin America (estimated share: 6%)
Latin America is an emerging market with growing demand from food and beverage and pharmaceutical sectors. Brazil and Mexico are key contributors, with growth of 5-6% annually. The region faces challenges from economic volatility and infrastructure gaps, but rising consumer incomes and e-commerce are driving adoption. Direction: Emerging growth potential.
Middle East & Africa (estimated share: 4%)
The Middle East and Africa are nascent markets with growth driven by healthcare expansion and food processing investments. The region is expected to grow at 4-5% annually, with the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and South Africa as key markets. Import dependence is high, and local manufacturing is limited. Direction: Gradual expansion.

Pharma Associations.url_match_title: KM Pharmaceutical targets global oral care market with Pororo products - The Korea Times
Pharma Associations.content:
Company sees new opportunity in low-fluoride toothpaste
KM Pharmaceutical Production Director Hwang Min-young shows the company's toothpastes designed with Pororo characters, inside the company's office in Pyeongtaek, Gyeonggi Province, Thursday. Courtesy of KM Pharmaceutical
PYEONGTAEK, Gyeonggi Province — KM Pharmaceutical, a hygiene product developer has created a sensation in Korea’s oral care market with its Pororo-themed toothpastes and toothbrushes.
The company, which is based in Pyeongtaek, Gyeonggi Province, is now seeking to replicate that success overseas. KM Pharmaceutical already exports to 12 countries as an original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and original development manufacturer (ODM) specializing in oral care, hair care and beauty products, but the company believes its overseas business still has significant room to grow.
The company has recently begun operating its second manufacturing plant in Pyeongtaek which is dedicated to hair care and beauty products. The expansion readied stronger exports for the company which aims to hit an annual sales goal of 100 billion won ($72 million).
“The second factory is now at full capacity and the first one about 70 percent. But considering the volume of orders we are receiving, the first factory will probably have to run at full speed as well,” said Hwang Min-young, production director of KM Pharmaceutical.
The company’s main businesses are OEM and ODM services for client firms, such as producing Pororo lineup, and manufacturing its private brands, including hair care label Zerocipe and oral care label Foamgle. The OEM and ODM volume now occupies more than 50 percent of the entire operation, with the Pororo lineup being KM Pharmaceutical’s exclusive products using the intellectual properties of animation content developer Iconix in Korea.
Shampoo products go through a packaging process at KM Pharmaceutical's second manufacturing plant in Pyeongtaek, Gyeonggi Province, Thursday. Courtesy of KM Pharmaceutical
KM Pharmaceutical’s overseas client base is growing. One of its recent clients is Swiss oral care company Weleda, for which KM began production early last year.
“Weleda has never manufactured outside its prime plant in Germany for the past century," Hwang said. "We are the first company outside Germany to produce for Weleda, including toothpastes for children and adults."
KM Pharmaceutical is currently in talks for an OEM and ODM deal with companies in the United Kingdom, Japan, the United States and Malaysia, with Zerocipe and Foamgle undergoing discussion for a market launch at Amazon and TikTok shop in the countries. The fact that the Korean company is catering to large-size pharmaceutical firms in Korea with OEM and ODM services has been a significant part of earning trust from potential partners, Hwang said.
“We have passed ISO standards, good-manufacturing-practices, and conditions for the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. But another thing we stand out for is that we are doing many OEM orders for large-size firms here," Hwang said.
"That means our manufacturing practices and end-products passed evaluations from our clients each year. Based on that fact, the foreign clients understand our OEM and ODM capabilities are being consistently verified. K-beauty and Korean oral care products generating buzz in global markets also adds to the foreign firms’ interest in us,” Hwang said.
KM Pharmaceutical President Brian Baik speaks during an interview with The Korea Times at the company's office in Pyeongtaek, Gyeonggi Province, Thursday. Courtesy of KM Pharmaceutical
KM Pharmaceutical’s goal is to become the country’s second-tier OEM and ODM company, behind industry giants Cosmax and Kolmar Korea. Its short-term goal is to achieve 50 billion won in annual sales by 2028, and later to reach 100 billion won.
KM Pharmaceutical President Brian Baik is optimistic about the goals. The company’s productivity this year jumped 11 percent from last year and its rising number of clients has pushed the firm’s monthly production volume to 2.1 million for oral products, 1.7 million for hair care products and 400,000 for beauty products. By 2028, the company expects its overall production capacity will increase by up to 150 percent from current capacity.
One of the opportunities KM Pharmaceutical is focusing on is the introduction of a new core ingredient for toothpaste. The company said hydroxyapatite is increasingly being considered overseas as an alternative to fluoride amid health concerns over excessive fluoride exposure.
“Fluoride toothpastes are widely used in Korea and even recommended by doctors. But that does not mean fluoride is completely risk-free,” Baik said. “The permitted fluoride content in toothpaste was initially limited to 1,000 parts per million (ppm) and was later raised to 1,450 ppm. Because toothpaste is used several times a day, some consumers may be concerned about the cumulative effects of fluoride exposure. There should be alternatives for people who prefer fluoride-free toothpaste.”
Demand for low-fluoride and fluoride-free toothpastes has been growing in the U.S. and Europe, but the trend is only beginning to emerge in Korea, where regulations on the use of hydroxyapatite in toothpaste have yet to be established.
KM Pharmaceutical said it plans to consult with the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety on whether hydroxyapatite can be used as a main ingredient in place of fluoride.
